one_line: Demonstrates how chin augmentation visually reduces perceived nose size using a split-screen comparison and pixel-change data.

hook.what_happens: A split-screen slider compares a woman's face before and after, asking if her nose is too big.
hook.why_it_works: It challenges the viewer's visual perception immediately with a relatable insecurity.

shots.description: Split-screen comparison of a woman's face with a sliding divider showing 'Before' and 'After'.
Heatmap overlay showing pixel changes on the face, accompanied by a bar chart.
Visual breakdown of facial proportions with circular callouts on the nose and chin.
Interactive text prompt instructing the viewer to perform a physical action.
Side-by-side comparison of the original and modified faces.
Final call to action with a search bar mockup.

transcript.text: Think your nose is too big? Same face. Same nose. Same woman, twice.
Same nose, both photographs. But it looks smaller in the second.
Her chin is what moved. Here is every pixel that changed.
Almost none of it is on her nose. Your eye doesn't measure features.
It compares them. When the chin sits back, the nose stands out.
Your brain calls it a big nose. Bring it forward and the nose has something to sit against.
It didn't shrink. The face caught up. Try it right now.
Push your lower jaw forward. Hold it there. Watch your nose.
Your nose just got smaller. You didn't touch it.
The question was never which feature to fix. It's what the whole face does when one thing moves.
See it on your own face first. A preview, not a promise. Search Refina AI.

narrative_arc: Introduce the common insecurity of a 'large nose' and challenge it with a visual comparison.
Reveal that only the chin was modified, leaving the nose completely untouched.
Provide scientific proof via pixel-change data to validate the claim.
Explain the optical illusion of facial proportions and how the brain compares features.
Engage the viewer with a physical, real-time experiment to prove the concept on themselves.
Direct the viewer to use the AI tool to preview these changes on their own face.

cta.what: Search 'Refina AI' to preview facial adjustments on your own face.

subjects: Unnamed woman acting as the visual model for the facial comparison.
what_makes_it_work: The interactive 'try it now' segment physically proves the optical illusion to the viewer instantly.
Data-driven visualization (pixel heatmap) adds scientific credibility to the visual claim.
